## Appointment of a special advocate

## 76.23

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.23] (1) Subject to paragraph (2), the Secretary of State must immediately give notice of the proceedings to the Attorney General upon –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.23] (a) making an application under section 4(1) of the Act (relating to a derogating control order);

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.23] (b) making an application under section 3(1)(a) of the Act (application for permission to make a non-derogating control order);

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.23] (c) making a reference under section 3(3) of the Act (reference of a non-derogating control order made without permission); or

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.23] (d) being served with a copy of any application, claim, or notice of appeal in proceedings to which this Part applies. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.23] (2) Paragraph (1) applies unless–

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.23] (a) the Secretary of State does not intend to –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.23] (i) oppose the appeal or application; or

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.23] (ii) withhold closed material from a relevant party; or

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.23] (b) a special advocate has already been appointed to represent the interests of the relevant party in the proceedings and that special advocate is not prevented from communicating with that party by virtue of rule 76.25. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.23] (3) Where notice is given to the Attorney General under paragraph (1), the Attorney General may appoint a special advocate to represent the interests of the relevant party in the proceedings. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.23] (4) Where any proceedings to which this Part apply are pending but no special advocate has been appointed, a relevant party or the Secretary of State may request the Attorney General to appoint a special advocate. ## Functions of special advocate

## 76.24

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.24] The functions of a special advocate are to represent the interests of a relevant party by –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.24] (a) making submissions to the court at any hearings from which the relevant party and his legal representatives are excluded;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.24] (b) adducing evidence and cross-examining witnesses at any such hearings; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.24] (c) making written submissions to the court. ## Special advocate: communicating about proceedings

## 76.25

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.25] (1) The special advocate may communicate with the relevant party or his legal representative at any time before the Secretary of State serves closed material on him. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.25] (2) After the Secretary of State serves closed material on the special advocate, the special advocate must not communicate with any person about any matter connected with the proceedings, except in accordance with paragraph (3) or a direction of the court pursuant to a request under paragraph (4). [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.25] (3) The special advocate may, without directions from the court, communicate about the proceedings with –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.25] (a) the court;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.25] (b) the Secretary of State, or any person acting for him;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.25] (c) the Attorney General, or any person acting for him; or

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.25] (d) any other person, except for the relevant party or his legal representative, with whom it is necessary for administrative purposes for him to communicate about matters not connected with the substance of the proceedings. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.25] (4) The special advocate may request directions from the court authorising him to communicate with the relevant party or his legal representative or with any other person. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.25] (5) Where the special advocate makes a request for directions under paragraph (4) –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.25] (a) the court must notify the Secretary of State of the request; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.25] (b) the Secretary of State must, within a period specified by the court, file with the court and serve on the special advocate notice of any objection which he has to the proposed communication, or to the form in which it is proposed to be made. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.25] (6) Paragraph (2) does not prohibit the relevant party from communicating with the special advocate after the Secretary of State has served material on him as mentioned in paragraph (1), but–

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.25] (a) the relevant party may only communicate with the special advocate through a legal representative in writing; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.25] (b) the special advocate must not reply to the communication other than in accordance with directions of the court, except that he may without such directions send a written acknowledgment of receipt to the legal representative of the relevant party. ## Modification of the general rules of evidence and disclosure

## 76.26

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.26] (1) Part 31 (disclosure and inspection of documents), Part 32 (evidence) and Part 33 (miscellaneous rules about evidence) do not apply to any proceedings to which this Part applies. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.26] (2) Subject to the other rules in this Part, the evidence of a witness may be given either –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.26] (a) orally, before the court; or

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.26] (b) in writing, in which case it shall be given in such manner and at such time as the court directs. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.26] (3) The court may also receive evidence in documentary or any other form. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.26] (4) The court may receive evidence that would not, but for this rule, be admissible in a court of law. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.26] (5) Every party shall be entitled to adduce evidence and to cross-examine witnesses during any part of a hearing from which he and his legal representative are not excluded. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.26] (5A) A special advocate shall be entitled to adduce evidence and to cross-examine witnesses. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.26] (6) The court may require a witness to give evidence on oath. ## Filing and service of relevant material

## 76.27

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.27] The Secretary of State is required to make a reasonable search for relevant material and to file and serve that material in accordance with the rules in this Part. ## Closed material

## 76.28

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.28] (1) The Secretary of State –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.28] (a) must apply to the court for permission to withhold closed material from a relevant party or his legal representative in accordance with this rule; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.28] (b) may not rely on closed material at a hearing on notice unless a special advocate has been appointed to represent the interests of the relevant party. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.28] (2) The Secretary of State must file with the court and serve, at such time as the court directs, on the special advocate –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.28] (a) the closed material;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.28] (b) a statement of his reasons for withholding that material from the relevant party; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.28] (c) if he considers it possible to summarise that material without disclosing information contrary to the public interest, a summary of that material in a form which can be served on the relevant party. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.28] (3) The Secretary of State may at any time amend or supplement material filed under this rule, but only with–

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.28] (a) the agreement of the special advocate; or

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.28] (b) the permission of the court. ## Consideration of Secretary of State’s objection

## 76.29

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (1) This rule applies where the Secretary of State has –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (a) objected under rule 76.25(5)(b) to a proposed communication by the special advocate or to the form in which it is proposed to be made; or

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (b) applied under rule 76.28 for permission to withhold closed material. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (2) The court must fix a hearing for the Secretary of State and the special advocate to make oral representations, unless –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (a) the special advocate gives notice to the court that he does not challenge the objection or application;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (b) the court has previously considered –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (i) an objection under rule 76.25(5)(b) to the same or substantially the same communication, or

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (ii) an application under rule 76.28(1) for permission to withhold the same or substantially the same material, and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] is satisfied that it would be just to uphold that objection or to give permission without a hearing; or

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (c) the Secretary of State and the special advocate consent to the court deciding the issue without a hearing. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (3) If the special advocate does not challenge the objection or the application, he must give notice of that fact to the court and the Secretary of State within 14 days, or such other period as the court may direct, after the Secretary of State serves on him a notice under rule 76.25(5)(b) or material under rule 76.28(2). [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (4) Where the court fixes a hearing under this rule, the Secretary of State and the special advocate must before the hearing file with the court a schedule identifying the issues which cannot be agreed between them, which must –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (a) list the items or issues in dispute;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (b) give brief reasons for their contentions on each; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (c) set out any proposals for the court to resolve the issues in contention. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (5) A hearing under this rule shall take place in the absence of the relevant party and his legal representative. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (6) Where the court gives permission to the Secretary of State to withhold closed material, the court must –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (a) consider whether to direct the Secretary of State to serve a summary of that material on the relevant party or his legal representative; but

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (b) ensure that no such summary contains information or other material the disclosure of which would be contrary to the public interest. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (7) Where the court has not given permission to the Secretary of State to withhold closed material from, or has directed the Secretary of State to serve a summary of that material on, a relevant party or his legal representative –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (a) the Secretary of State shall not be required to serve that material or summary; but

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (b) if he does not do so, at a hearing on notice the court may –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (i) if it considers that the material or anything that is required to be summarised might be of assistance to the relevant party in relation to a matter under consideration by the court, direct that the matter be withdrawn from its consideration, and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (ii) in any other case, direct that the Secretary of State shall not rely in the proceedings on that material or (as the case may be) on what is required to be summarised. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.29] (8) The court must give permission to the Secretary of State to withhold closed material where it considers that the disclosure of that material would be contrary to the public interest. ## Order of filing and serving material and written submissions

## 76.30

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.30] Subject to any directions given by the court, the parties must file and serve any material and written submissions, and the special advocate must file and serve any written submissions, in the following order –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.30] (a) the Secretary of State must file with the court all relevant material;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.30] (b) the Secretary of State must serve on

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.30] (i) the relevant party or his legal representative; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.30] (ii) the special advocate (as soon as one is appointed) or those instructing him,

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.30] any open material;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.30] (c) the relevant party must file with the court and serve on the Secretary of State and special advocate (if one is appointed) or those instructing him any written evidence which he wishes the court to take into account at the hearing;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.30] (d) the Secretary of State must file with the court any further relevant material;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.30] (e) the Secretary of State must serve on –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.30] (i) the relevant party or his legal representative, and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.30] (ii) the special advocate (as soon as one is appointed) or those instructing him,

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.30] any open material filed with the court under paragraph (d);

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.30] (f) the Secretary of State must serve on the special advocate (if one has been appointed) any closed material;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.30] (g) the parties and the special advocate (if one has been appointed) must file and serve any written submissions as directed by the court. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.30] (Rules 76.28 and 76.29 will apply where any closed material is filed by the Secretary of State). ## Failure to comply with directions

## 76.31

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.31] (1) Where a party or the special advocate fails to comply with a direction of the court, the court may serve on him a notice which states –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.31] (a) the respect in which he has failed to comply with the direction;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.31] (b) a time limit for complying with the direction; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.31] (c) that the court may proceed to determine the proceedings before it, on the material available to it, if the party or the special advocate fails to comply with the relevant direction within the time specified. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.31] (2) Where a party or special advocate fails to comply with such a notice, the court may proceed in accordance with paragraph (1)(c). ## Judgments

## 76.32

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.32] (1) When the court gives judgment in any proceedings to which this Part applies, it may withhold any or part of its reasons if and to the extent that it is not possible to give reasons without disclosing information contrary to the public interest. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.32] (2) Where the judgment of the court does not include the full reasons for its decision, the court must serve on the Secretary of State and the special advocate a separate written judgment including those reasons. ## Application by Secretary of State for reconsideration of decision

## 76.33

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.33] (1) This rule applies where the court proposes, in any proceedings to which this Part applies, to serve notice on a relevant party of any –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.33] (a) order or direction made or given in the absence of the Secretary of State; or

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.33] (b) any judgment. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.33] (2) Before the court serves any such notice on the relevant party, it must first serve notice on the Secretary of State of its intention to do so. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.33] (3) The Secretary of State may, within 5 days of being served with notice under paragraph (2), apply to the court to reconsider the terms of the order or direction or to review the terms of the proposed judgment if he considers that –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.33] (a) his compliance with the order or direction; or

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.33] (b) the notification to the relevant party of any matter contained in the judgment, order or direction;

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.33] would cause information to be disclosed contrary to the public interest. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.33] (4) Where the Secretary of State makes an application under paragraph (3), he must at the same time serve on the special advocate, if one has been appointed –

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.33] (a) a copy of the application; and

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.33] (b) a copy of the notice served on the Secretary of State pursuant to paragraph (2). [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.33] (5) Rule 76.29 (except for paragraphs (6) and (7)) shall, if a special advocate has been appointed, apply with any necessary modifications to the consideration of an application under paragraph (3) of this rule. [PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.33] (6) The court must not serve notice on the relevant party as mentioned in paragraph (1) before the time for the Secretary of State to make an application under paragraph (3) has expired. ## Supply of court documents

## 76.34

[PART 76 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE PREVENTION OF TERRORISM ACT 2005 > 76.34] Unless the court otherwise directs, rule 5.4 (Register of Claims), rule 5.4B (Supply of documents from court records – a party) and rule 5.4C (Supply of documents from court records – a non-party) do not apply to any proceedings to which this Part applies.
